Confucianism quotes

Confucianism is a family of ethical and political teachings centered on humaneness, ritual propriety, learning, and the cultivation of character in relationships.

73 passages · 13 voices in this archive selection

Overview

From Confucius and Mencius to Xunzi and later Neo-Confucians such as Zhu Xi and Wang Yangming, the tradition debates human nature, education, and rightful government while sharing a concern for moral formation through practice.

Historical notes

Classical Confucianism emerges in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods; imperial China institutionalized Confucian learning; modern New Confucians reinterpret the tradition for contemporary societies.

Core ideas

  • Ren (humaneness) and li (ritual) shape ethical life.
  • Learning and self-cultivation are lifelong.
  • Family and political roles are moral arenas.
  • Debate continues on whether nature is good (Mencius) or needs shaping (Xunzi).

FAQ

What is Confucianism?

It is a tradition of ethical and political thought emphasizing humaneness, ritual, education, and cultivated character.

Who are key Confucian thinkers?

Confucius, Mencius, and Xunzi are classical pillars; Zhu Xi and Wang Yangming are major Neo-Confucians.

Where can I read Confucian quotes in English?
